clauses.reason: Statutory pay systems: sets the rates of basic pay of the statutory pay systems on the attached schedules. Ends when EO 12984 (signed 1995-12-28; 61 FR 237, Federal Register of January 3, 1996) in its Sec. 7: supersedes EO 12944: "Sec. 7. Prior Order Superseded. Executive Order No. 12944 of December" "28, 1994, is superseded." The sentence carries no delayed-effective-date wording of its own, so the end is the signing date, 1995-12-28. Alternative reading disclosed: the successor order's schedules take effect on the first day of the first pay period on or after January 1, 1996, so this order's rates may be read as governing pay until then; that is not a single stated date, and the express supersession sentence is the first held instrument ending the order.

Supersedes EO 12826 of December 30, 1992 and EO 12886 of December 23, 1993. A supersession of whole earlier orders is a one-time act; the order states no effective date for this sentence (Sec. 6 fixes dates only for the schedules), so it was performed on signing, 1994-12-28, and the command is exhausted on that date. A later supersession of EO 12944 does not change when this one-time command was performed.

research_rationale:
EO 12944 of December 28, 1994 (Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay and Allowances), read in full in the held Federal Register text (60 FR 309, Federal Register of January 3, 1995; machine-extracted text layer). Identity: number, date and subject agree with the census register row (1994-12-28). The order sets pay-system schedules (Sec. 1 to 4, Schedules 1 to 8), interim geographic adjustments (Sec. 5, Schedule 9) and effective dates (Sec. 6), and its Sec. 7 supersedes EO 12826 and EO 12886; the dossier lists 19 clauses and I confirm them as the operative inventory (the enacting formula is not a separate command; the clause listed as item 7 under Sec. 3(c) is an OCR fragment of the Schedule 7 reference). EO 12984 (signed 1995-12-28) supersedes this order expressly in its Sec. 7. The dossier flagged a located-provision gap for EO 12945; I read EO 12945 in full: it amends EO 12640 on Vice Chairs of the President's Committee on Employment of People with Disabilities and does not name this order. Searches: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts) were chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no scope warning. Machine hits for this order: current-law:usc 0, current-law:ecfr 0, later-events:ofr_catalog 3. The packet's by-number scan of held order texts (LOOKUPS) was read for this order; held texts citing this number are its own text and EO 12984, the superseding order.
